stories.headline: Meta Commits Additional $21B to CoreWeave for AI Cloud Infrastructure Through 2032

key_facts.fact: Meta committed an additional $21 billion in spending with CoreWeave on AI cloud infrastructure, on top of a prior $14.2 billion arrangement disclosed in September 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta has made a $21 billion commitment to AI cloud provider CoreWeave, adding to a prior arrangement of $14.2 billion.

key_facts.fact: The new agreement runs from 2027 to 2032, while the previous deal goes through 2031.
key_facts.excerpt: The new agreement, announced on Thursday, runs from 2027 to 2032. The previous deal, disclosed in September, goes through 2031.

key_facts.fact: CoreWeave's data centers are filled with hundreds of thousands of Nvidia GPUs and the company also serves Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI.
key_facts.excerpt: CoreWeave's data centers are filled with hundreds of thousands of Nvidia graphics processing units that can accommodate AI models… While Meta and its peers are building out their own facilities, they need capacity from companies like CoreWeave, which also serves Google, Microsoft, OpenAI and others.

key_facts.fact: Meta plans to spend between $115 billion and $135 billion on capital expenditures in 2026, nearly twice its 2025 capex.
key_facts.excerpt: In Meta's last earnings report, the company said it plans to shell out between $115 billion and $135 billion this year in capital expenditures, above Wall Street's estimates and nearly twice the amount it spent on capex in 2025.

key_facts.fact: After the new deal, no single CoreWeave customer will represent more than 35% of total sales, down from Microsoft's 62% share of 2024 revenue, CEO Mike Intrator said.
key_facts.excerpt: The new business will help CoreWeave further diversify away from Microsoft, which represented 62% of its 2024 revenue. Now no customer will represent more than 35% of total sales, Intrator said.

key_facts.fact: CoreWeave held $21 billion in debt at the end of 2025 and borrowed an additional $8.5 billion in March 2026 to add infrastructure tied to new contracts.
key_facts.excerpt: CoreWeave, which went public last year, held $21 billion in debt on its balance sheet at the end of 2025, and in March borrowed another $8.5 billion to add infrastructure tied to new contracts.

key_facts.fact: Meta has partnered with CoreWeave since 2023; CEO Mike Intrator said Meta's portfolio approach reflects that 'there's just too much risk not to' use CoreWeave alongside its own data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: "They're going to continue to do it themselves, but they're also going to continue to do it with us," CoreWeave CEO Mike Intrator said in an interview. "There's just too much risk not to."

sources.title: Meta commits to spending additional $21 billion with CoreWeave

stories.headline: TSMC's CoWoS Advanced Packaging Grows at 80% CAGR as Nvidia Reserves Most Capacity

key_facts.fact: TSMC's most advanced chip packaging method currently in use, Chip on Wafer on Substrate (CoWoS), is growing at an 80% compound annual growth rate, according to the company's North America packaging head Paul Rousseau.
key_facts.excerpt: Its most advanced method currently in use is called Chip on Wafer on Substrate, or CoWoS, and Rousseau said it is increasing at a stunning 80% compound annual growth rate.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia has reserved a majority of the most advanced packaging capacity available at TSMC, which is the volume leader in advanced packaging.
key_facts.excerpt: AI giant Nvidia has reserved a majority of the most advanced capacity available at TSMC, which is the volume leader in packaging.

key_facts.fact: TSMC is building its first U.S. advanced packaging facilities in Arizona this year and is ramping up two new packaging sites in Taiwan.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC is building its first U.S. advanced packaging facilities in Arizona this year, and ramping two new sites in Taiwan.

key_facts.fact: Almost all advanced packaging — the chip-making step that connects multiple small chips into a final GPU — currently happens in Asia, forcing chips manufactured in the U.S. to be shipped to Taiwan for packaging before returning.
key_facts.excerpt: Every microchip used to power artificial intelligence must be put into hardware that can interact with the outside world. But right now, almost all of this chipmaking step, known as advanced packaging, happens in Asia, and capacity is in short supply.

key_facts.fact: Intel is technologically on par with TSMC on packaging and counts Amazon and Cisco as customers; on April 7, Elon Musk also tapped Intel to package custom chips for SpaceX, xAI and Tesla at the planned Terafab plant in Texas.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel is technologically on par with the Taiwanese giant. The U.S. chipmaker has struggled to solidify a major external customer for its chip fabrication business, but its packaging customers include Amazon and Cisco. On Tuesday, Musk also tapped Intel to package custom chips for SpaceX, xAI and Tesla at his ambitious Terafab plant planned for Texas.

key_facts.fact: Georgetown CSET researcher John VerWey warned advanced packaging 'can emerge as a bottleneck very quickly' if companies don't make proactive capex investments to handle the surge in fab output coming in the next couple of years.
key_facts.excerpt: "It can emerge as a bottleneck very quickly if people are not making the CapEx investments proactively to account for the surge in fab output that's going to be coming in the next couple of years," said John VerWey of Georgetown University's Center for Security and Emerging Technology.

sources.title: Nvidia snaps up AI chip packaging capacity as TSMC expands in U.S.

stories.headline: OpenAI Pauses Stargate UK Data Center Project, Citing High Energy Costs and Regulation

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said on Thursday it is pausing its Stargate AI infrastructure project in the UK, citing the high cost of energy and the regulatory environment.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is pausing its Stargate infrastructure project in the UK, citing the high cost of energy and regulatory environment.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said it 'will move forward when the right conditions such as regulation and the cost of energy enable long-term infrastructure investment.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We see huge potential for the UK's AI future," the company said in an emailed statement on Thursday. "AI compute is foundational to that goal — we continue to explore Stargate UK and will move forward when the right conditions such as regulation and the cost of energy enable long-term infrastructure investment."

key_facts.fact: Stargate UK was announced in September 2025 as a partnership with Nvidia and UK data center operator Nscale, with a plan to host approximately 8,000 Nvidia AI processors at Cobalt Park on Tyneside in the first quarter of 2026, scaling to up to 31,000 GPUs over time.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI will explore offtake up to 8,000 GPUs in Q1 2026 with the potential to scale to 31,000 GPUs over time… the project is expected to be based across a number of sites, including Cobalt Park, which will form part of the newly designated AI Growth Zone in the North East.

key_facts.fact: The Q1 2026 deadline for Stargate UK passed without construction beginning, and OpenAI declined to offer a revised timetable in early April.
key_facts.excerpt: The initial plan envisaged housing approximately 8,000 Nvidia AI processors at Cobalt Park on Tyneside during the first quarter of 2026. That deadline has now passed without a spade in the ground, and OpenAI has declined to offer a revised timetable.

key_facts.fact: Up to 50% of large data center projects globally are running behind schedule due to planning problems and energy constraints, according to research by Sightline Climate.
key_facts.excerpt: Research by Sightline Climate indicates that up to half of all large-scale data centre projects are now running behind schedule, hampered by planning difficulties and constraints on energy supply.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced the Stargate UK project in September 2025 alongside other US tech investments during President Trump's state visit to the UK; the ruling Labour party has placed AI at the centre of its growth strategy.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI announced the project in September, part of a wave of investments from American technology giants during Donald Trump's visit to the UK. The ruling Labour party has made…

stories.headline: Alibaba and China Telecom Launch AI Data Center With 10,000 Homegrown Zhenwu Chips

key_facts.fact: Alibaba and China Telecom launched a data center in Shaoguan, Guangdong province, powered by 10,000 of Alibaba's self-developed Zhenwu AI chips, designed for AI training and inferencing.
key_facts.excerpt: The facility, announced on Tuesday, will feature 10,000 of Alibaba's Zhenwu semiconductors which are designed for AI training and inferencing along with the ability to support AI models the size of hundreds of billions of parameters. China Telecom will own and operate the data center.

key_facts.fact: The cluster is designed to support training of AI models with hundreds of billions of parameters and is expected to expand to a scale of 100,000 chips.
key_facts.excerpt: China Telecom and Alibaba said the data center, located in Shaoguan, in the Guangdong province of China, is expected to expand to a scale of 100,000 chips. The computing cluster can be used in industries from healthcare to advanced materials, they added.

key_facts.fact: The new cluster delivers a 30% improvement in training and inference efficiency, with individual card throughput up nearly tenfold versus previous-generation systems and end-to-end network latency held to 4 microseconds.
key_facts.excerpt: The company reported that the new cluster's advanced high-performance networking framework, which allows all 10,000 chips to function as a unified supercomputing system, delivers a 30% improvement in training and inference efficiency. Individual card throughput has seen a nearly tenfold jump compared to previous-generation systems, with network latency held to a critical 4 microseconds for enterprise applications.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba's Zhenwu chips were developed by its T-Head semiconductor unit and the launch follows the activation last month of a Huawei Ascend 910C-based computing cluster, both responding to U.S. export restrictions on Nvidia AI chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba, one of China's largest tech firms, has been designing its own chips through its T-head unit… Last month, a computing cluster built with Huawei's advanced Ascend 910C AI chips went online.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu announced creation of a new technology committee to 'accelerate' the company's AI development, which he will head alongside Chief AI Architect Zhou Jingren, Alibaba Cloud CTO Li Feifei, and Alibaba Group CTO Wu Zeming.
key_facts.excerpt: On Tuesday, Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu announced the creation of a technology committee which he will head. Joining him on the committee will be the company's Chief AI Architect Zhou Jingren, Chief Technology Officer of Alibaba Cloud Li Feifei, and Wu Zeming, chief technology officer for Alibaba Group. The organizational changes were made to 'accelerate' Alibaba's AI development, Wu said, according to a memo seen by CNBC.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba's stock rose nearly 8% on the data center news as Beijing intensifies its push for self-sufficient AI infrastructure under its 15th five-year plan.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba's stock rose nearly 8% on the news… Last month, Beijing formally incorporated intelligent computing infrastructure into its 15th five-year plan.

sources.title: Alibaba launches data center in China with its own AI chips
Alibaba and China Telecom Deploy Major AI Data Center with 10,000 Homegrown Chips

stories.headline: Arm CEO Rene Haas Set to Lead SoftBank International Business to Advance Project Izanagi AI Chip Strategy

key_facts.fact: Arm CEO Rene Haas is in line to lead much of SoftBank Group's international business while keeping his current role as head of Arm, according to a Financial Times report citing people familiar with the matter.
key_facts.excerpt: Rene Haas, the chief executive of UK chip designer Arm, is in line to lead a swath of SoftBank Group's international business, the Financial Times reported on Thursday, citing multiple people familiar with the matter. Haas would take on the new role alongside his position as the head of Arm, the report said.

key_facts.fact: The new role would include oversight of operations in semiconductors, artificial intelligence and possibly robotics, designed to advance SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son's ambitions in semiconductors and AI.
key_facts.excerpt: The new role, which Haas would assume while maintaining his position as head of Arm, would include oversight of operations in semiconductors, artificial intelligence and possibly robotics, the FT reported, citing multiple people familiar with the matter. The move is designed to advance SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son's ambitions in semiconductors and AI.

key_facts.fact: The expanded responsibilities would enable Haas to advance Project Izanagi, SoftBank's AI chip strategy aimed at competing with established rivals such as Nvidia.
key_facts.excerpt: The expanded responsibilities would enable Haas to advance Project Izanagi, SoftBank's AI chip strategy aimed at competing with established rivals such as Nvidia.

key_facts.fact: Haas was expected to take a title reflecting his senior role at SoftBank Group International, but was not expected to run the company's Vision Fund investment vehicles or its energy business.
key_facts.excerpt: Haas was expected to take a title reflecting his senior role at SoftBank Group International, but was not expected to run the company's Vision Fund investment vehicles or its energy business, the report added.

key_facts.fact: The new role has not yet received approval from the boards of SoftBank and Arm, according to the Financial Times.
key_facts.excerpt: The new role has not yet received approval from the boards of SoftBank and Armm the FT reported.

key_facts.fact: Last month Arm unveiled a new AI data centre chip that it said would add billions of dollars in revenue and mark a significant shift in strategy; its shares are up more than 10% since the announcement.
key_facts.excerpt: Last month, Arm unveiled a new artificial intelligence data centre chip, which it said would add billions of dollars in revenue and mark a significant shift in strategy. Its shares are up more than 10% since the announcement.

stories.headline: China's UniX AI Begins Global Deliveries of Panther Wheeled-Dual-Arm Humanoid Robot for Households

key_facts.fact: Suzhou-based UniX AI unveiled Panther, its third-generation full-size wheeled dual-arm humanoid robot, and commenced global deliveries, marking what it called a major milestone in bringing service humanoid robots into real homes.
key_facts.excerpt: UniX AI, a global humanoid robotics service provider… has unveiled Panther, its all-new third-generation full-size wheeled dual-arm humanoid robot series. Alongside the recent release of a video demonstrating its humanoid robot in a real household setting, UniX AI has also commenced global deliveries of Panther, marking a major milestone in bringing service humanoid robots into real homes.

key_facts.fact: Panther is fitted with what UniX AI calls the world's first mass-produced 8-degrees-of-freedom bionic arms, an adaptive intelligent gripper, and an omnidirectional four-wheel steering and four-wheel drive (4WS+4WD) chassis.
key_facts.excerpt: The all-new wheeled dual-arm humanoid robot Panther is fitted with the world's first mass-produced 8-DoF bionic arms, an adaptive intelligent gripper on its high-DOF joint platform and features an omnidirectional four-wheel steering and four-wheel drive (4WS+4WD) chassis.

key_facts.fact: Panther features 34 high-DoF joints, an 80 cm vertical lift of the upper body to enable ground-level operation, and is built on a 48V power platform to deliver more output and stability for high-speed control.
key_facts.excerpt: UniX AI's next-gen humanoid robot Panther features 34 high-DoF joints, the world's first mass-produced 8-DoF bionic arms, and adaptive intelligent grippers… An 80 cm upper-body lift enables ground-level reach… Powered by an upgraded 48 V platform and a new power architecture, Panther offers stronger output, greater mobility, and higher stability.

key_facts.fact: Panther stands 1600-1750mm tall, has dual-arm load capacity of 12 kg, single-arm reach of 982 mm, repeatability of ±0.5 mm, and a four-wheel drive chassis with a movement speed of 2 m/s.
key_facts.excerpt: Full-size with a height of 1600-1750mm… 8-DoF Bionic Arm Dual-arm Load Capacity: 12kg Single-arm Reach: 982mm Repeatability: ±0.5 mm Chassis System Four-Wheel Steering And Four-Wheel Drive Omnidirectional Chassis… Movement Speed: 2m/s

key_facts.fact: UniX AI deliberately chose a wheeled dual-arm architecture over the dominant legged-locomotion approach used by competitors, prioritizing 'usability, real-world applications, and customer experience' for commercial environments and complex indoor service scenarios.
key_facts.excerpt: UniX AI has adopted a wheeled dual-arm architecture solution for its Panther humanoid robot rather than the current dominant approach of combining legged locomotion with a general-purpose foundation model… Rather than seeking to build the 'most human-like robot,' UniX AI prioritizes usability, real-world applications, and customer experience to deliver superior stability, flexibility, and task execution efficiency in today's commercial environments.

sources.title: UniX AI introduces Panther, the world's first service humanoid robot to enter real household deployment

stories.headline: U.S. Air Forces Central Orders $9M+ in Skydio Autonomous Dock Drones to Secure Middle East Airbases

key_facts.fact: Skydio announced an order exceeding $9 million from U.S. Air Forces Central (USAFCENT) for Skydio Dock and X10 systems to secure U.S. airbases across the Middle East — one of the largest autonomous drone infrastructure deployments for international base security by the U.S. Air Force.
key_facts.excerpt: Skydio… today announced an order exceeding $9M from U.S. Air Forces Central (USAFCENT), the air component of U.S. Central Command (USCENTCOM), for Skydio Dock and X10 systems to secure U.S. airbases across the Middle East–one of the largest autonomous drone infrastructure deployments for international base security by the U.S. Air Force.

key_facts.fact: Skydio Docks deployed at strategic positions across airbases enable fully remote operation, launching X10 drones in under 20 seconds to patrol, verify, and respond to security threats, with a single operator able to manage multiple drones simultaneously.
key_facts.excerpt: Deployed at strategic positions across airbases, Skydio Docks enable fully remote operation, launching X10 drones in under 20 seconds to patrol, verify, and respond to security threats. A single operator manages multiple drones simultaneously, maintaining a common operating picture across the installation while reducing personnel requirements.

key_facts.fact: When integrated sensors detect a threat, Skydio drones launch immediately and stream live high-definition and thermal video to the Base Defense Operations Center until the incident is resolved.
key_facts.excerpt: When integrated sensors alert, drones launch immediately, stream live high-definition and thermal video to the Base Defense Operations Center (BDOC), and maintain continuous visual contact until the incident is resolved.

key_facts.fact: The X10D is the most widely deployed Group 1 Unmanned Aircraft System for USAF Security Forces and is the small UAS of choice for Air Combat Command Tactical Air Control Party Specialists and PACAF Security Forces.
key_facts.excerpt: Skydio X10D is the most widely deployed Group 1 UAS for USAF Security Forces, selected as the sUAS of choice for Air Combat Command (ACC) Tactical Air Control Party Specialists (TACP) and PACAF Security Forces (A4S).

key_facts.fact: Skydio is trusted by every branch of the U.S. military and the armed forces of 29 allied nations, with all drones and docking systems produced at its facility in Hayward, California.
key_facts.excerpt: Skydio is trusted by every branch of the U.S. military and the armed forces of 29 allied nations. Every drone and docking system is produced at Skydio's facility in Hayward, California.

key_facts.fact: The contract follows a $52 million U.S. Army order in March 2026 for over 2,500 Skydio X10D drones — the largest single-manufacturer small UAS purchase in Army history.
key_facts.excerpt: The US Army has placed an order worth over $52m with US drone manufacturer Skydio to supply more than 2,500 X10D small uncrewed aircraft systems (sUAS)… the contract was awarded in less than 72 hours from the initial bid and represents the largest single-manufacturer sUAS purchase in the Army's history.

sources.title: U.S. Air Forces Central selects Skydio Dock to secure U.S. airbases in the Middle East
